summary: Audited 12,875 full-coverage claims across 6 historical runs (MSFT, SNDK x2, MU, NVDA, AMD, replayed through the current architecture via comqutor_alpha.replay). 3,050 claims contained relation-like language from the required phrase families; of those, only 20 resolved 2+ canonical factors yet produced zero relation candidates. Manual review labeled 18/20 CORRECTLY_REJECTED and 2/20 AMBIGUOUS_REQUIRES_REVIEW. Zero claims met the TRUE_RELATION_MISSED bar. No candidate rule reached the promotion threshold (>=3 independent TRUE_RELATION_MISSED claims across >=2 agents/runs/tickers, OR a standard-syntax pattern with 2 positive + 3 hard-negative fixtures and 0 new false positives). Per the task's own explicit instruction, no relation/factor production code was modified in response to this finding.
discovery_set: SNDK (both the latest 2026-07-27 run and the 2026-07-17 run) -- 2 of the 20 flagged candidates originate from SNDK runs.
validation_set: MSFT, MU, NVDA, AMD (4 independent historical runs) -- 18 of the 20 flagged candidates originate here.

candidates_considered.pattern: Intro clause + colon + 'If X, Y' conditional, where the conditional marker is not clauses[0] of the whole claim
candidates_considered.why_not_promoted: Below the >=3-independent-claims-across->=2-sources bar (only 1 occurrence, 1 agent, 1 run, 1 ticker); no hard-negative fixtures have been written or tested for this pattern; promoting on a single example risks widening the CONDITIONAL rule family's clause-anchoring in a way that has not been checked against any negative case.
candidates_considered.known_limitations: This is a real, plausible rule-family gap (colon-prefixed intro clause before a conditional) worth revisiting once more examples accumulate across future runs.

candidates_considered.pattern: 'reduce'-family verb with its two factor mentions split across a relative-clause boundary ('X, which could reduce Y')
candidates_considered.why_not_promoted: Only 1 occurrence in the entire 12,875-claim, 6-run corpus. The audit script's own endpoint identification for this row is a naive heuristic (first two distinct factors mentioned in the claim), not a confirmed grammatical parse -- the true source/target pairing has not been manually confirmed as correct. Promoting a cross-clause-reach widening from one unverified example would risk exactly the kind of generalization-beyond-evidence the task explicitly prohibits.
candidates_considered.known_limitations: Needs a second, independently-sourced example (different agent/run/ticker) with a manually-confirmed source/target pairing before this is even a well-formed rule proposal.
